**Current forecasts from MetService, Met Office, and other sources point to a maximum of 13°C in Wellington on August 21, 2026, with some model runs allowing for 14°C under clearer conditions.** 

August climatology shows typical daily highs of 12–14°C (around 54°F), reflecting the Southern Hemisphere winter baseline with frequent southerly flows. Recent NIWA guidance indicates near-average temperatures are most probable, following earlier cold polar air outbreaks that have now given way to high-pressure settling and lighter northerlies. This setup supports modest daytime warming without strong frontal systems, keeping the distribution tightly clustered around the 13–14°C outcomes that dominate trader pricing. Minor forecast revisions in the next model runs could shift odds between these two leading results, while extremes remain improbable given the stable synoptic pattern.

eventMetadata.context_description: National Weather Service guidance and ensemble models position 98–99°F as the most likely peak for Houston on August 21 under a persistent high-pressure ridge promoting mostly sunny skies, light southerly flow, and dew points in the mid-70s that limit cooling. Recent observations confirm a regional heat wave with heat indices near 106–108°F, consistent with late-summer climatology when afternoon highs commonly reach the upper 90s. Model consensus shows limited spread around 97–100°F, supporting the market’s heavy weighting on the 98–99°F bin while assigning lower probability to 100–101°F outcomes absent stronger subsidence or clearer skies. Updated NHC and local office briefings ahead of the 21st will refine these projections.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model runs from AEMET and ECMWF place Madrid’s August 22 high near 33–34 °C under mostly clear skies and light northerly flow, after a mid-month cooldown from peaks above 35 °C. Ensemble spread remains tight because daytime heating depends on subtle differences in boundary-layer mixing, surface insolation, and the precise arrival of any weak Atlantic trough. Madrid’s urban heat island and high plateau elevation amplify maximum temperatures once skies clear, while even modest increases in low-level moisture or wind speed can cap readings one degree lower. Traders therefore assign nearly equal weight to the two leading outcomes, reflecting the narrow scientific uncertainty in the final 48-hour forecast window.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 22 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Active southwest monsoon conditions dominate trader sentiment for Manila's August 22 high temperature, with PAGASA forecasting a 32°C peak amid 70% rain chance from enhanced convection and cloud cover that limits surface heating. Market-implied odds cluster tightly on 31°C (37%) and 32°C (30.5%) because typical August maxima hover near 30–31°C under Habagat-driven humidity and frequent showers, while brief clear spells or reduced rainfall could allow brief spikes to 33°C. Key variables include monsoon strength, localized thunderstorm timing, and urban heat retention, with fresh PAGASA model runs and satellite observations likely to refine resolution criteria over the next 48 hours.
